name: Imperative Negation with do-support

1.details: Uses do-support for negation in imperatives, even when an auxiliary could negate in declaratives.

constraints.description: Negation is expressed with do-support (do not/don't) in imperatives.

relatedConstructions.notes: Negative imperative retains imperative clause type and its special do-support requirement

projection.target: A prohibitive imperative can use don’t with be, as in Don’t be late, while an ordinary finite declarative uses She isn’t late. The negative inclusive Let’s not leave instantiates a different imperative subtype.
projection.evidence: CGEL documents the distinctive imperative do distribution and the order alternatives in negatives with let’s.

curious.title: Telling someone not to
curious.summary: To tell someone not to do something, English uses don't or do not, even with be.
curious.body:
Don't look at me and Don't be afraid are negative commands. Don't comes first, and the rest follows.

The pattern uses don't even where a plain statement wouldn't. A statement uses She isn't late, but a negative command uses Don't be late. A speaker can add you for emphasis, as in Don't you look at me!, or use a word like everyone, as in Don't everyone shout it out.
curious.try: Tell a friend not to be late, then not to be noisy. Do you say don't each time?

teacher.summary: Teaches negative commands with don't, including the contrast with be in declaratives.
teacher.explain: A prohibitive imperative uses do-support for negation: Don't look at me. This dictionary notes this holds even with be, where an auxiliary could negate in a declarative: Don't be afraid, against She isn't late. An overt subject can follow don't, as in the emphatic Don't you look at me! and in a quantified subject such as Don't everyone shout it out. The negative inclusive Let's not leave is a different imperative subtype. This dictionary marks its analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: Do-support is the usual name. Prohibitive imperative is this dictionary’s term for a negative command.
watch_for: A learner might negate be in an imperative as in a declarative, when this dictionary requires do-support.
A learner might treat Let's not leave as the same subtype as Don't be late.
A learner might place an overt subject before don't instead of after it.
teacher.activity: Give students positive commands including some with be. They turn each into a negative command, then contrast with a statement such as She isn't late.

child.hook: How do you tell someone not to do something?
child.explain: You can start with Don't. Don't look at me is a negative command. Don't be afraid uses Don't too, even with be.
child.play: Tell your partner five things not to do, starting with Don't. Include one with be, like Don't be late.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Imperative Negation with do-support." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/imperative-negation-do-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, fa37529).
